periods.analysis: Harborview paid 98.4% of invoices within 30 days in 2024-Q3, establishing a strong green baseline against the >=95% target. From a control perspective, the result reflects disciplined use of three-way match in the Tyler Munis AP queue and timely department approvals, especially on the Public Works and Parks vendor routes. The volume mix included summer field work, police fleet maintenance, and recreation programming invoices, but no material aging pocket emerged in the 21-30 day band. I would not call this automatic performance; it is the product of close cutoff management and clean vendor master data.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the weekly AP aging huddle and keep the 21-day exception report going to department fiscal liaisons every Tuesday. Extend vendor portal enrollment to the remaining high-volume local suppliers, starting with the top 25 by invoice count. Finance should also document the Q3 cutoff checklist as the standard control file for the next close.

periods.analysis: The rate moved down 0.9 points from 98.4% to 97.5% in 2024-Q4, still comfortably green and above the >=95% target. The decline is understandable given year-end purchasing, grant closeout documentation, and a heavier construction retainage review cycle in December. AP staff kept the exposure contained by prioritizing invoices already past day 20 and by routing larger purchase-order exceptions through the FIN-AP-14 escalation log. The main control note is that holiday schedules made approver availability the limiting factor, not cash capacity or system throughput.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the year-end approver backup roster and require each department to name a secondary approver before the first December purchasing freeze date. Extend the FIN-AP-14 escalation log to include reason codes for retainage, missing receiving, and contract amendment delays. Keep green performance protected by pre-loading known recurring Q4 invoices for utilities, software renewals, and fleet leases.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q1, performance declined another 1.2 points from 97.5% to 96.3%, but remained green. The quarter carried the aftereffects of Q4 accrual cleanup and several new-year blanket purchase orders that required revalidation before invoices could be released. I am watching the pattern because two consecutive declines can hide process drift even when the headline number is above target. The AP team’s manual review of vendor banking changes was appropriate from a fraud-control standpoint, though it added time to a small set of payments.
periods.recommendations: Hold the manual bank-change control, but add a same-day callback target for low-risk returning vendors so fraud prevention does not become avoidable aging. Run a cohort review of invoices delayed by new blanket PO setup and send the results to Procurement by commodity code. Sustain the green result by keeping daily triage on invoices at day 24 or higher until the downward trend is reversed.

periods.analysis: The measure improved 0.4 points from 96.3% to 96.7% in 2025-Q2, a useful stabilization while remaining green. The recovery appears tied to earlier PO setup for seasonal paving, marina maintenance, and recreation contracts, which reduced preventable match exceptions. Finance also benefited from the April vendor master cleanup, where duplicate records for several small service vendors were merged before invoice routing. The improvement is modest, but it shows the controls can be tightened without slowing the payment cycle.
periods.recommendations: Make the April vendor master cleanup a quarterly control, with a signed exception memo for any duplicate vendor record left open. Extend early PO setup to all seasonal departments by publishing a 45-day procurement readiness calendar before summer work begins. Continue tracking match-exception aging separately from ordinary approval aging so we can see which control is driving any future slippage.

periods.analysis: Harborview rose 0.7 points from 96.7% to 97.4% in 2025-Q3, keeping the measure green and moving back toward the stronger starting range. Summer invoice volume was high, but AP used department-specific worklists for Public Works crews, lifeguard operations, and facilities repair vendors to keep approvals moving. The new receiving checklist for field supervisors reduced the number of invoices held for missing packing slips or service confirmations. This is the kind of improvement I trust because it is tied to a repeatable control, not a one-time push at quarter end.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the department-specific AP worklists and formally assign an owner in each operating department for invoices over day 15. Extend the field supervisor receiving checklist to Police fleet, IT hardware, and Facilities on-call trades. Finance should sample 30 paid invoices from the Q3 worklists to verify that speed did not compromise authorization, match, or segregation-of-duties controls.

periods.analysis: The rate fell 1.6 points from 97.4% to 95.8% in 2025-Q4, still green but much closer to the >=95% floor than I prefer. The movement coincided with year-end contract amendments, insurance renewal invoices, and a heavier capital-project pay application review cycle. We did not lose control of the process, but the cushion narrowed enough that I would treat the quarter as a control-warning signal inside a green result. The specific watch item is approver latency on invoices requiring both project manager certification and Finance contract review.
periods.recommendations: Create a Q4 dual-approval dashboard showing invoices waiting on project manager certification versus Finance contract review, with owners named at day 18. Sustain the green status by continuing daily AP aging review during the December close window rather than reverting to twice-weekly review. For next Q4, require departments to submit contract amendments at least 10 business days before expected invoice receipt.

periods.analysis: Performance improved 0.8 points from 95.8% to 96.6% in 2026-Q1, moving away from the target floor and remaining green. The rebound reflects tighter January restart discipline, including pre-cleared recurring payments for utilities, software, and lease obligations. AP also separated true invoice defects from simple approval delays in the AP-RISK-07 tracker, which made follow-up more precise. That said, the rate is still below the 2025-Q3 level of 97.4%, so I would characterize this as a controlled recovery rather than a full reset.
periods.recommendations: Keep the AP-RISK-07 tracker and use it at month-end to report the top five delay causes by department. Extend pre-clearance of recurring payments to annual maintenance and public safety service agreements where contract terms are stable. Maintain a minimum two-person review of invoices released after day 25 so catch-up activity does not weaken payment controls.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q2, Harborview increased 0.5 points from 96.6% to 97.1%, preserving green performance and confirming the recovery trend. The result shows that the Q1 control adjustments held through spring purchasing, including street resurfacing mobilization, marina supplies, and permit-system support invoices. The payment process is again operating with a healthier cushion above the >=95% target, though not at the 98.4% baseline seen in 2024-Q3. I view the current posture as financially sound and operationally controlled, provided we continue to manage exceptions before they age into the last week.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the weekly aging huddle, AP-RISK-07 cause tracking, and department worklists as the standard operating model through the next fiscal year. Extend vendor portal adoption to any supplier with more than 12 invoices annually, with Procurement adding portal participation language to new bid packets. Set an internal management watch line at 96.0% so corrective action starts before the public target is at risk.

periods.analysis: The available figure is 97.1% paid within 30 days, above the 95% target. It is carried forward from June rather than a new September close.
periods.recommendations: Keep the weekly aging review and reconcile the September AP extract before presenting a quarter-end change.
